speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your bleeding issues, can you tell me if you have a family history of bleeding disorders or if you are currently taking any medications like aspirin or blood thinners?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history and your symptoms, have you ever experienced bleeding into your joints, such as pain or swelling in your knees or elbows? I also need to know if you have a history of prolonged bleeding after other minor injuries or surgeries.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those details. The history of joint swelling in your uncle, combined with your easy bruising and persistent post-extraction bleeding, strongly suggests a clotting factor deficiency like Hemophilia. I will now order specific coagulation studies to confirm the diagnosis. speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's presentation of persistent mucosal bleeding (post-extraction) and easy bruising, combined with a family history suggestive of an X-linked or autosomal dominant trait, points toward a clotting disorder. Given the prolonged PTT and the lack of personal hemarthrosis, von Willebrand disease is the most likely diagnosis, as it is the most common inherited bleeding disorder and often presents with mucocutaneous bleeding rather than deep joint bleeds.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Von Willebrand Disease
